ORDER With the consent of both the parties the matter is heard finally.

This miscellaneous appeal under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed challenging the impugned award dated 11.07.2016 passed in claim case No.284/2013 by Eighth Additional Member, MACT, Indore.
In which the application of the appellant was partly allowed.

sentences.text: Operation was conducted and the fracture was fixed by inserting implant.

3. In view of the above minimum compensation amount of Rs.25,000/- could have been granted in this case but the Claims Tribunal has not awarded any amount for the aforesaid injuries as the doctor was not examined to prove the injuries suffered by the claimant, but the medical report and the X-Ray report (Exhibit P-9) on record proves the injury suffered by the claimant.
4. Learned counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance Company has fairly submitted that the Claims Tribunal has not awarded any amount under the head of grievous injury.
5. On this limited point heard the appeal and perused the record of the claimant in Ex. P-4.
The claimant was 17 years old at the time when incident took place.

As per the MLC report of Bafna Hospital she suffered injuries and as per Ex.P-9 i.e X-ray report grossly comminuted fracture upper 1/3rd and mid 1/3rd right tibia was found and as per the medical report attached with the record the fractured bone was fixed by surgery and implant.
6. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and the nature of injuries the claimant was entitled for minimum of Rs.25,000/- as compensation.
7. Due to fracture in the right leg the claimant shall have suffering and pain for life long though not economically but it will affect her life expectancy.
She will be devoid of pleasures of life due to her injuries.
8. In the facts and circumstances of case, the nature of injury and age of the claimant Rs.40,000/- is awarded under the head of grievous injury.
9. With the above observations the claim is enhanced to Rs.40,000/- and the compensation amount is enhanced to that extent.

The respondent No.3/Insurance Company shall deposit this enhanced amount of Rs.40,000- within two months from the date of passing of this order and in default the Insurance Company shall also pay the above amount with simple interest @ 9% per annum from the date of order till the amount is deposited.
The respondent No.3/Insurance Company shall bear the costs of the appeal.
Thus, with the above directions, the Miscellaneous Appeal stands disposed off.
Registry is directed to verify whether the Court fee is properly deposited by the applicant or not and if not the applicant is directed to deposit the deficit Court fee, within time.
Then only the Registry shall sent the original record back to the Tribunal.
C.c as per Rules.
(DEVNARAYAN MISHRA) JUDGE akanksha Ku. Sanjna Thru.
